URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/reform-uk-farage-support-labour-tories-ipsos-poll-b3072895.html
The Independent — datePublished and dateModified both 2026-10-25T10:30:04Z = 10:30 GMT Sun 25 Oct. Retrieved by curl at 17:35 GMT. Pollster is IPSOS, which is on the approved list. Electoral Calculus, also approved, supplies the seat projection.

HEADLINE SENSE: Reform UK support has collapsed to 20 per cent, putting the Conservatives in clear second on 24, with Labour on its best rating since the 2024 election.

THE NUMBERS
Labour 32 per cent — "its biggest poll rating since the last election".
Conservatives 24 per cent.
Reform UK 20 per cent — "the Tories four points ahead of them", the Conservatives' biggest lead over Reform since the 2024 general election.
Electoral Calculus projection on these figures: a Labour majority of 134, "slightly down on the 167 majority they won in July 2024". [Flag: Labour's actual 2024 Commons majority is usually given as 174 (411 seats of 650). The Independent's "167" is Electoral Calculus's own figure as reported and should not be restated as the historical record without checking.]
Cross-check against the same paper's 16:13 GMT Budget piece: Labour "eight points ahead of the Tories and 12 points above a Reform UK on the slide" — 32-24=8 and 32-20=12. Internally consistent.

ON THE RECORD — IPSOS
Keiran Pedley, Ipsos research director: "Whilst the headline figures do show a striking change, they confirm a pattern we have been seeing in the underlying data for some time." / "The Labour Party under Andy Burnham is resurgent, consolidating voters on the left behind them." / "On the right, the tectonic plates have been shifting recently and now this is reflected in the Conservatives - not Reform UK - being in a clear second place." / "However, we should be mindful against overreacting to one poll." / "The government faces a challenging Budget this coming week and the lesson of the last year is that British politics is volatile. The picture today is very different to six months ago and it could be different again in six months' time too."
Note the self-limiting caveat: Pedley explicitly warns against overreacting to one poll. Any use of this should carry it.

CONTEXT CARRIED BY THE INDEPENDENT
"A year ago Reform was polling at above 30 per cent and Mr Farage was favourite to become prime minister at the next election." A YouGov poll last week showed voters no longer consider Reform a "main party".
Reform's run of difficulties as listed: a parliamentary standards commissioner investigation into a £5m donation to Farage from Christopher Harborne; police investigations into deputy leader Richard Tice and Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick; the resignation of chief of staff Dan Jukes and policy director James Orr after a Channel 4 investigation into illegal donations; an ITV investigation into racism among candidates and councillors. Channel 4 and ITV are approved outlets but these are characterisations of their work, not retrieved from them.
Raheem Kassam, described as a key Farage ally, attacked the poll: "I suspect this isn't actually very good data but on the off chance that it is accurate, I will have no sympathy for the Britons who vote for the uniparty and then endure the worst decade they've ever experienced between now and 2036. The capital flight will be astounding. You'll be begging for foreign aid in rather than dishing it out."
